title: Dry electrode manufacturing at scale
bottleneck: Dry electrode coating eliminates toxic NMP solvent and energy-hungry drying ovens, but making uniform, well-adhered thick electrodes without solvent is still unreliable: dry-mixed powders suffer from binder distribution problems, calendering cracks, and inconsistent porosity. Tesla's 4680 dry-cathode ramp famously struggled for years with yield, showing how hard the process is even with massive resources.
why_it_blocks: Wet coating lines are capital-intensive and energy-hungry, adding meaningful cost and carbon footprint to every cell. Dry processing could cut electrode manufacturing cost and emissions substantially — if yields ever match wet lines.
current_state: Dry anode coating is now routine at some manufacturers, but dry cathode at automotive yields remains elusive outside limited production. The process window is narrow and chemistry-specific, so each new cathode formulation restarts the learning curve.
